summary.title: 7 Common Mistakes in Architecture Diagrams
summary.one_liner: Seven frequent pitfalls in technical architecture diagrams (theoretical diagrams, mixed abstraction levels, busyness, unlabeled arrows, misleading nesting, missing context, and no explainer text) and how to fix each.
keywords: how to make clear architecture diagrams
split busy diagram into multiple diagrams
takeaways: Prefer concrete diagrams of your own system over generic theoretical ones, since generic versions already exist online.
Keep resources at the same abstraction level in one diagram, and split high- and low-level views into separate diagrams.
Every arrow should carry a label unless the relationship is obvious from repetition or overlap.
Avoid nesting that implies false containment (e.g., availability zones inside a VPC); use a dashed outline or move the element to another view.
Pair diagrams with prose explaining why design choices were made, since diagrams show what but not why.
summary.summary: The post, written by the Ilograph team, lists seven common mistakes in technical architecture diagrams and gives a fix for each. Examples include mixing high-level and low-level resources, cramming too many concerns into one view, and unlabeled arrows. It also covers misleading box nesting in AWS diagrams, missing context for newcomers, and relying on diagrams without explanatory text. The advice is illustrated with diagram screenshots (not available in the page text), and it points to a follow-up article with seven more mistakes.
